Subject: Recap & next actions — deployment pathway and dedicated sizing asks

Hi Sarah — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a dedicated path and compare Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for your use case.

High-level: Cobble is prioritizing low 200ms p50 for short chat prompts, and a batch of longer-generation workflows for content synthesis (avg 1,800 tokens). You mentioned a steady baseline of ~120 TPS for chat (mostly <128 tokens) with peaks up to 600 TPS during batch jobs.

Questions we need to finalize sizing:
- Confirm steady-state TPS: is 120 TPS the 24/7 baseline or a regional baseline?
- Peak duration: are the ~600 TPS peaks sustained (minutes/hours) or short spikes?
- Token mix: percent of requests <128 tokens vs >1024 tokens (estimate).
- Latency SLO: p50/p95 targets for interactive chat (you said p50 ~200ms).
- Data locality/compliance: would Cobble require VPC/private control plane or is a hosted solution acceptable for the pilot?

What we recommend next:
1) Attach your sample traffic export (if available) so we can run a short capacity pro forma — I included a template for token profile: deployment_token_profile.csv (attached).
2) Ben + Marissa to propose a GPU mix recommendation (A100/H100 tradeoffs) and an ops checklist for dedicated sizing.
3) Schedule a 45-min ops sync next week to walk through POC plan (microbenchmark + ingress shaping).

Attachments: deployment_token_profile.csv (please fill), but if you can forward the traffic export from your analytics team that would accelerate sizing.

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben + Marissa on the technical asks.

—

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers below and I attached the traffic snapshot (cobble_traffic_export_q3.csv) from our metrics team.

- Baseline 120 TPS is a global baseline (average across US regions) — in EU we see ~15% of that during business hours.
- Peaks to 600 TPS are typically sustained for ~20–40 minutes (batch runs + marketing spikes). We have occasional larger spikes (1,200 TPS) during launches but those are rare (~1/month).
- Token mix (approx): 75% of requests <128 tokens, 20% between 128–1024, 5% >1024 (these are long content synth jobs).
- Latency target: p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 600ms for interactive flows. For long jobs we accept higher latency but want predictable throughput.
- Compliance: for the pilot hosted is fine, but production may require Private VPC depending on procurement.

I attached cobble_traffic_export_q3.csv. Happy to jump on a call — Tue/Wed next week works for us.

Thanks for the data, Sarah — good visibility. Quick technical read and initial recommendation for a Dedicated path (pilot):

Summary of constraints from the export: baseline ~120 TPS (global), 20–40m sustained peaks to 600 TPS, token distribution matches Sarah’s note. Interactive SLO p95 budget ~600ms.

Initial Dedicated recommendation (pilot):
- GPU family: Recommend H100-based pool for the pilot if you need headroom for peaks and better perf for long sequences — H100 gives ~20–40% better throughput vs A100 for our kernel mix on long-token workloads. If cost is the primary concern and peaks are short, A100 80GB is still viable.
- Instance mix: start with 4x H100 nodes (8 cards total if using 2x GPUs per node) to cover baseline + burst with autoscale to add 2 nodes for sustained peaks. We’ll run microbenchmarks against your token mix to validate TPS.
- Concurrency & batching: target request concurrency per GPU ~6–12 (we’ll tune continuous batching). For short chat flows we’ll favor lower latency paths (smaller batches, KV cache enabled). For long batch jobs, route to quantized instances with larger batch windows.
- Quantization: consider qat/8-bit for the inference pipeline for long jobs to reduce cost; keep FP16 fast path for interactive traffic to preserve quality.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated system/prompt tokens — should reduce effective token compute by ~8–12% for your mix.

Ops asks for sizing pro forma:
1) Confirm expected sustained peak duration frequency (so we can model autoscale economics).
2) Provide any hard SLO penalties (if procurement asks for credits).
3) If Private VPC is probable, we’ll include uplift for private control plane and KMS integration (will add 8–12% to infra effort).

I’ve attached a short note with the assumption matrix: gpu_recommendation_notes.txt. Next steps: Naomi — if we get a quick microbenchmark slot (we can do 2–3 hours), we’ll produce an empirical TPS map and a recommended node count + cost delta between H100/A100 paths.
